headline: GOLD BOUNCES FROM $3,426 15-MONTH LOW — Lower Yields Open Path to $3,740 Recovery Despite 97.5% December Fed Hike Odds
snippet: Spot gold is attempting a recovery from the $3,426 15-month low struck this week, with FX Empire citing a pullback in 10-year Treasury yields as the near-term catalyst. Analysts set $3,740 as the first meaningful resistance target, though December Fed hike odds remain locked near 97.5% following October's hotter-than-expected 3.3% core PCE reading.

headline: CHILE DOUBLES LITHIUM INVESTMENT TO $10.8B IN RECORD COCHILCO PLAN — $111.1B 2026-2035 Mining Portfolio Hits 13-Year High; Lithium Accounts for 92% of Growth
snippet: Chile's mining investment body Cochilco has released its 2026-2035 portfolio at a record $111.1 billion — the largest in 13 years — with lithium investment more than doubling to $10.8 billion and accounting for 92% of the portfolio's growth. Copper still dominates at 84.5% of total value, but the surge in lithium projects reflects the global energy transition demanding Chile accelerate its brine-and-hard-rock pipeline beyond the Atacama.

headline: HSBC WARNS GOLD COULD FALL TO $3,000 — 3.3% Core PCE Locks In December Fed Hike as HSBC Cuts Year-End Target
snippet: HSBC issued a bearish gold outlook after October core PCE came in at 3.3%, cementing market expectations for a December 8-9 Federal Reserve rate hike at nearly 97.5% odds. The bank warns gold could decline to $3,000 if the Fed signals additional hikes in January, citing the 10-year real yield sitting above 1.5% as the key headwind for the non-yielding metal.

headline: EMPEROR METALS RETURNS 18.7m AT 3.0 G/T GOLD AT DUQUESNE WEST — 4.5m at 10.4 g/t Near-Surface High Grade in Quebec; Visible Gold Hits at 190m Down-Hole
snippet: Emperor Metals (CSE: AUOZ) has returned 18.7 metres grading 3.0 g/t gold including a 4.5-metre interval at 10.4 g/t from near-surface drilling at the Duquesne West gold project in Quebec's Abitibi. Visible gold was also intercepted at 190 metres down-hole in a hole drilled 1.5 km east of the main pit area, hinting at a larger system than current resource outlines suggest.

headline: FURY GOLD INTERCEPTS 9.81 G/T IN SEVEN MINERALIZED ZONES AT EAU CLAIRE — James Bay Resource Conversion Drilling Confirms Geological Continuity
snippet: Fury Gold Mines (TSX/NYSE American: FURY) has released Phase 2 resource conversion drill results from Eau Claire in James Bay, Quebec, with highlight intervals including 9.81 g/t gold over 2.99 metres within seven separate mineralized zones. The company describes the holes as targeting portions of the current Inferred Mineral Resource where geological continuity has already been demonstrated, underscoring a methodical path toward an updated resource estimate.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING DRILLS 111.15m AT 5.48 G/T AuEq FROM SURFACE AT APOLLO — Tungsten-Enriched High-Grade Zone Expands Colombia Porphyry Footprint
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) has reported 111.15 metres averaging 5.48 g/t gold equivalent from surface drilling at the Apollo system within its Guayabales project in Colombia, the program's widest near-surface interval to date. The result includes a tungsten-enriched subzone and extends the near-surface high-grade footprint ahead of a planned maiden mineral resource estimate in early 2027.

headline: LME BASE METALS MOSTLY RETREAT ON NOVEMBER 27 — Copper Stays Near 11-Month Lows as Macro Headwinds Override Bargain Buying
snippet: LME base metals gave back a portion of Wednesday's gains in Thursday's session, with copper remaining pinned near 11-month lows around $5.38-$5.40 per pound as market participants weighed a prolonged Federal Reserve rate-hike cycle against still-resilient demand signals from Chinese smelters. Manganese ore bucked the trend with higher sales volume, while prices across the base metals complex were broadly rangebound.

headline: DRC COBALT BAN HANDS PRICING POWER TO ALTERNATIVE SUPPLIERS — Western Cobalt Assets in Australia, Canada and Philippines Emerge as Near-Term Beneficiaries
snippet: Crux Investor argues that Congo's November 30 cobalt export suspension structurally redirects procurement toward the handful of non-DRC cobalt suppliers still capable of meaningful output — primarily from Australia, Canada, and the Philippines. The analysis identifies cobalt producers and royalty holders outside the DRC as near-term beneficiaries as off-take contracts require emergency rerouting.

headline: GOLD STRUGGLES FOR TRACTION AS FED HIKE BETS DOMINATE — Real Yields Above 1.5% Explain Miners' Stubborn Discount to Spot Metal
snippet: FXStreet's November 26 analysis explains why gold cannot hold any recovery: with the 10-year Treasury at 4.85% and core PCE at 3.3%, real yields have climbed above 1.5%, a level that historically correlates with significant gold underperformance. The piece also contextualises gold miners' unusual gap to spot — earnings remain near-record but equity prices have collapsed 29-49% in three months as investors rotate to yield-bearing alternatives.

headline: COBALT WEEKLY: DRC BAN DRIVES RALLY FROM EXPECTATIONS INTO TRANSACTION VALIDATION — SMM Asks How Far the Surge Can Run
snippet: Shanghai Metals Market's weekly cobalt review notes that the market has shifted from price gains driven by anticipation of the DRC export suspension to actual transactional price validation, as buyers began paying up ahead of the November 30 effective date. SMM analysts question how durable the rally is given that stockpiles outside the DRC — particularly in China and the Netherlands — could supply refiners for several months before a physical shortage bites.
